report.summary: Across 90 exported entries (89 distinct video IDs), Beyond the Blackwall primarily presents cyberpunk/sci-fi music for tabletop roleplay, dystopian writing, focus and atmospheric listening. Individual songs commonly use a distinctive name plus genre/mood descriptor, often separated by //; named long-form collections commonly use ||. The recurring scene-setting opening is a stronger channel signature than the generic copied hashtags. Long-form chapters and tracklists are useful but inconsistent. All exported YouTube tag arrays are empty, so genre tags proposed here are recommendations, not observed tag-field usage. The export contains no engagement analytics or thumbnail pixels.

observedConventions.pattern: A distinctive song name is followed by a double-slash separator and descriptive genre, mood, or listening use case; this is the dominant individual-track naming pattern.
examples: Devils Bunker // Cyberpunk Industrial Combat Music
Dying Breath // Industrial Synthwave Combat Music
Friday Night Firefight // Techno Metal Cyberpunk Combat Music

observedConventions.pattern: Named collections use a volume/series name followed by a double-pipe separator and a descriptive mix genre; some explicitly include runtime.
examples: Hyperspace Traveller Vol 1 || Sci-Fi Power Metal & Retro Synth Mix
Neon Shallows Vol. 2 || Chill Lo-fi Cyberpunk Ambiance 1hr
Neon Shallows Vol. 1 || Cyberpunk 80s Synthwave Mix 1hr 20m

observedConventions.pattern: Descriptions repeatedly identify tabletop sessions, science-fiction writing, focus/study/coding, and retrowave/dark-synth listeners as intended uses.
examples: Cyberpunk RED / Shadowrun sessions
Sci-fi & dystopian writing
Focus / study / coding playlists

observedConventions.pattern: Many individual tracks begin with a short bespoke mood, scene, or purpose line, often starting with Music for or Music to, followed by reusable audience text.
examples: Music for when the solution is belt fed.
Music for after the worst did happen
Music for the deep sea data divers

observedConventions.pattern: A fixed block of hashtags is repeated across most tracks, especially synthwave, cyberpunk, retrowave, outrun, TTRPG music, and AI-generation disclosure.
examples: #synthwave #cyberpunk #retrowave #outrun #ttrpgmusic #aestheticmusic #futuristicmusic #ai #aigenerated #ambiance

observedConventions.pattern: Individual uploads cover industrial combat, techno/darkwave, lo-fi/chill, synthwave, metal, jazz and vocal tracks rather than one uniform sound.
examples: Devils Bunker // Cyberpunk Industrial Combat Music
Think On It // Lo-fi Sad Dreamy Cyberpunk Ambience
Smoke and Truth - Cyberpunk Jazz Lounge with Female Vocals
Eat the Rich // Cyberpunk Rock / Metal Female Vocals

observedConventions.pattern: Some compilation descriptions include tracklists or timestamped YouTube chapters, with the long-form megamix providing an extensive timestamped example.
examples: Tracklist: 00:00 8 Bit Intro ...
Youtube Chapters 0:00 Neon Blossom ...
Youtube Chapters 0:00 Neuro ...

observedConventions.pattern: Short videos often reuse a full-track name and add Short, but the naming convention varies and some shorts reuse full-video descriptions.
examples: Dancing Green short
Victory Noods - Short
Neon Blossom Short

inconsistencies.issue: The export contains a duplicated video ID and identical record, which should not be counted as independent evidence.
The title separator varies among //, ||, |, hyphens and no separator; a consistent convention would improve automated titles.
Compilation descriptions vary from one generic sentence to comprehensive tracklists and listening-use descriptions.
Some descriptions are blank or malformed, including a short with a truncated opening.
A uniform synthwave hashtag block is reused even on jazz, metal, ska, and other non-synthwave recordings; the export contains no populated YouTube tags fields.
A few tracks are marked or described as vocal while the main reusable positioning often implies background ambience; metadata should accurately describe each new recording.

recommendations.recommendation: Use {project} || {genre} Mix ({duration}) for compilations, but omit the duration parentheses when the UI cannot verify runtime.
recommendations.rationale: This follows named collection uploads while making format and runtime clear. Duration must come from actual rendered media.

recommendations.recommendation: Use {track} // {genre} for individual tracks, optionally adding a short mood or use-case phrase when grounded in the music.
recommendations.rationale: This matches the dominant single-track title structure and avoids keyword stuffing.

recommendations.recommendation: Retain the bespoke one-line atmospheric opening and the tabletop/writing/focus audience positioning, adapting it to the actual release.
recommendations.rationale: These are distinctive established conventions; avoid automatically claiming every recording is suitable for every use.

recommendations.recommendation: Include verified crossfade-aware chapters in every compilation when available, and never fabricate timestamps.
recommendations.rationale: Existing long-form descriptions demonstrate the usefulness of chapters but their inclusion is inconsistent.

recommendations.recommendation: Use a small set of universal hashtags plus relevant genre-specific hashtags; keep AI disclosure when accurate and avoid copyrighted game or place names in new original branding.
recommendations.rationale: Current blanket hashtags are repetitive and sometimes unrelated to the track style.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not infer thumbnail appearance, performance, audience retention, or SEO effectiveness from this export.
recommendations.rationale: The dataset contains metadata but no image pixels, view counts, impressions, or audience analytics.

universalBranding.footer: Cyberpunk and science-fiction listening for tabletop sessions, dystopian writing, focus and late-night listening.
